newsitem.title: UK: Russia debt jumps as Yeltsin goes to work.
newsitem.headline: Russia debt jumps as Yeltsin goes to work.

text.p: Russia headed up a strong emerging debt market on Wednesday buoyed by the reported improvement in condition of President Boris Yeltsin, whose health has been the subject of a wave of rumours.
"The whole market is up and Russia is the strongest...Russia has been lagging and I think has quite a ways to catch up," Bank of America senior trader Michael Jordan said.
Vneshekonombank dollar debt RUVNUSLNS=RR was up 1/2 a point to just over 80 cents in the dollar.
The market has been plagued by rumours that Yeltsin, recovering from pneumonia, may have been dead and even this morning that he was about to quit office.
"Some shorts tried to spread rumours that Yeltsin, after going through hell to recover, was going to the Kremlin to give up his job. That was one of the funnier ones this morning," a trader said.
Yeltsin made his unexpected return to the Kremlin this morning shortly before parliament was due to debate a motion forcing him to step down because of ill health.
In the current bullish Brady market, its high yield has been enough to attract investors despite political chaos and serious concerns about its economic outlook.
A firmer U.S. Treasury market is the main factor pushing up Bradys for the moment, with support also coming in on the back of strong demand for Argentina's upcoming global bond.
